name: MMStar
description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans to evaluate large vision-language models' multi-modal capacities. MMStar covers 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, with carefully balanced and purified samples designed to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements.
creator: Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao, Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang
citeAs: Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao, Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models?
rai:dataCollection: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, then strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples. The curation criteria are: visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requiring advanced multi-modal capabilities for resolution. The source pool comes from six existing benchmarks, and after coarse filtering with LLM inspectors and manual review by three experts, the sample pool was reduced from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples and finally to 1,500 samples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark is constructed from samples selected from six existing benchmarks: MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista. The authors first choose two benchmarks focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge for sample collection.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors develop an automated pipeline to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet the criteria of visual dependency and minimal data leakage. They evaluate the sample pool with eight LLM inspectors and document the hit frequency for each evaluation sample. Only samples with hit counts of two or fewer are retained. They also tally the hit counts of 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The source sample pool is evaluated by two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs sized 20B or larger serving as inspectors. The open-source LLMs are applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting. Samples with hit counts of two or fewer are retained, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607. Then three experts manually review samples to ensure visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and advanced multi-modal difficulty, finally selecting 1,500 samples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conduct manual review to ensure each sample's answer should be based on understanding visual content, selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions, and most samples should require advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. The benchmark is organized into 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To expedite manual selection of samples with varying difficulty levels, the authors tally the hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). They also ensure each core capability contains a balanced 250 samples and a relatively even distribution across the 18 detailed axes.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper argues that inappropriate questions and data leakage can lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLMs. It states that for research to be transparent and equitable, it is imperative to account for and mitigate such leakage so that models are evaluated on their true ability to integrate and interpret multi-modal data rather than memorize samples.
rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two major issues in existing benchmarks: many samples lack visual dependency and can be answered from text alone or world knowledge, and unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training. These issues bias evaluation results and can cause unfair comparisons and misjudgments of real multi-modal gains.
rai:dataLimitations: Even with MMStar, the best evaluated model scores under 60 on average. The paper also notes that existing benchmarks often contain visual-unnecessary samples and leaked samples, which motivated MMStar. Future work is planned to expand MMStar into a larger online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods, implying current benchmark scale and static evaluation remain limitations.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models' multi-modal capabilities. It is used for evaluation/testing of LVLMs across 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, and for analyzing multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage with the proposed MG and ML metrics.
